title: Revolut Cuts AI Token Costs by 90% With Shift to Self-Hosted GLM for Engineering
summary:
Revolut transitioned approximately 2,000 of its engineers to a self-hosted GLM model for coding, moving previously used tools like Claude Code and Codex to an exception list. The system runs on 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs and costs a blended 30 cents per million tokens, which is about 10% of what the fintech firm paid for APIs from OpenAI and Anthropic.

David Abitbol, who leads AI operations at Revolut, stated the transition helped the company stop rationing tokens, allowing engineers to use AI for all tasks instead of only the most difficult tickets. The shift to an internal model reduced engineering lead time by 70%.

selectedTweets.text:
BREAKING: Revolut moved ~2,000 engineers onto self-hosted GLM for coding and pushed Claude Code and Codex to the exception list.

Per David Abitbol, who leads AI ops there: 56 Nvidia B200s, a blended 30 cents per million tokens, roughly a tenth of what they paid Anthropic and OpenAI. Engineering lead time improved 70%.

Here's the part that matters: the gains showed up when tokens stopped being rationed. Engineers quit saving AI for the hard tickets and pointed it at everything.

Frontier models become the exception, open weights become the default. That's a pricing problem for every lab heading to IPO.

h/t @OliverMolander

Would you move your team off frontier APIs if the bill dropped 90%?
